paragraphs.title: Targeting “BEST” Lifetime Value (LTV) Customers using Oracle Machine Learning
paragraphs.text:
%md
### Finding “BEST” Lifetime Value (LTV) Customers using Oracle Machine Learning

Heather has spent most of her time over the past couple of years extracting and preparing data for analysis. The large volumes of data need extracting and processing mean she spends most of her time waiting for jobs to finish and very little of her time analyzing the data. Demands from marketing are forcing a new approach whereby the data remains in the data warehouse and is processed there. The alternative cloud solution is more complex, and has no direct out of the box processes to analyze the data in place. She started taking a look at Oracle, and found the simple SQL commands in ADW are familiar, and execute extremely fast, leveraging all the performance features of the platform. Further once she is done can can apply the learning models to incoming data on the fly, and allow end user analysts to immediately see mining results. This drastically reduces the cycle of data preparation, analysis, and publishing. It also means there is no change to analysis/reporting Data Visualization toolset that users are familiar with.

Scroll down this notebook and learn how to use OML to create predictive perspectives on data in ADW, WITHOUT moving it. We will process a small 100k data set, but could use a 100M or billion row data set without worrying about processing time.

This is an extract of Alphaoffice customer information. We will first get acclimated to Apache Zepplin, the open source interface for interactive collaboration in a team environment.

%md
### The Business Problem:
#### Increase Sales by Targeting our Best Customers; High Lifetime Value Customers!
Heather has a hunch that weakening sales may be due to the company selling to non-optimal customers; customers who perhaps have poor credit and fail to make their payments for their purchases. Heather has over 100 variables to consider so wants to first explore her data using simple charts and graphs, but then move onto using Oracle Machine Learning's powerful algorithms to automtically sift through her data to find patterns, new insights and to make predictions that target her best customers–those who have good credit.

paragraphs.text:
%md
##### We have data of customers in table credit_scoring_100k with CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE as a numeric field. We would like to predict customer's lifetime value as High, Medium or Low and not as a numerical value. This gives us flexibilty to easily identify High Lifetime Value Customers and a company can focus on them. We will use this field to create a categorical field LIFETIME_VALUE_CATEGORY with values High/Medium/Low.

paragraphs.title: Check the distribution of CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE and label them as Low/Medium/High
paragraphs.text:
%sql

-- Group the Customers into High,Medium and Low valued Customers based on the CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE 


   SELECT COUNT(CUSTOMER_ID), range
   FROM(
        SELECT CUSTOMER_ID,
          CASE
          when CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE >= 0 AND CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE< 100000 THEN 'Low'
          when CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE >= 100000 AND CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE<300000 THEN 'Medium'
          ELSE 'High' END AS RANGE
        FROM CREDIT_SCORING_10K) t
    GROUP BY RANGE;

paragraphs.title: Update PREDICT_LTV_BIN to categorize customers as Low, Medium, High lifetime values
paragraphs.text:
%script

--Update PREDICT_LTV_BIN to categorize customers as Low, Medium, High lifetime values

UPDATE PREDICT_LTV_BIN
SET LIFETIME_VALUE_CATEGORY = 'High'
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_ID
        FROM CREDIT_SCORING_10K
        WHERE CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE >= 300000 and CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_ID = PREDICT_LTV_BIN.CUSTOMER_ID);

UPDATE PREDICT_LTV_BIN
SET LIFETIME_VALUE_CATEGORY = 'Medium'
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_ID
        FROM CREDIT_SCORING_10K
        WHERE CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE >= 100000 and CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE < 300000 and CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_ID = PREDICT_LTV_BIN.CUSTOMER_ID);

UPDATE PREDICT_LTV_BIN
SET LIFETIME_VALUE_CATEGORY = 'Low'
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_ID
        FROM CREDIT_SCORING_10K
        WHERE CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE >= 0 and CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_LIFETIME_VALUE < 100000 and CREDIT_SCORING_10K.CUSTOMER_ID = PREDICT_LTV_BIN.CUSTOMER_ID);

%sql

-- Delete the Null values from the Predict_LTV_BIN

DELETE FROM PREDICT_LTV_BIN

paragraphs.title: Hint
paragraphs.text:

paragraphs.title: Compute the Confusion Matrix for Random Forest
paragraphs.text:
%script

-- Compute the Confusion Matrix 

BEGIN EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'DROP TABLE ltv_bin_rf_confusion_matrix';
EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL; END;
/
DECLARE
    v_accuracy    NUMBER;
BEGIN
    DBMS_DATA_MINING.COMPUTE_CONFUSION_MATRIX (
        accuracy => v_accuracy,
        apply_result_table_name      => 'N1_APPLY_RESULT_RF',
        target_table_name            => 'N1_TEST_DATA_LTV',
        case_id_column_name          => 'customer_id',
        target_column_name           => 'lifetime_value_category',
        confusion_matrix_table_name  => 'ltv_bin_rf_confusion_matrix',
        score_column_name            => 'PREDICTION',
        score_criterion_column_name  => 'PROBABILITY',
        score_criterion_type         => 'PROBABILITY');
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('**** MODEL ACCURACY ****: ' || ROUND(v_accuracy * 100,4));
END;
/

paragraphs.title: Average Accuracy and Predictive Confidence for Random Forest
paragraphs.text:
%sql

-- Average Accuracy and Predictive Confidence

   WITH
    a as
      (SELECT a.actual_target_value, sum(a.value) recall_total
         FROM ltv_bin_rf_confusion_matrix a
         group by a.actual_target_value)
      ,
    b as
      (SELECT count(distinct b.actual_target_value) num_recalls
         FROM ltv_bin_rf_confusion_matrix b)
      ,
    c as
      (SELECT c.actual_target_value, value
         FROM ltv_bin_rf_confusion_matrix c
         WHERE actual_target_value = predicted_target_value)
      ,
    d as
      (SELECT NVL(sum(c.value/a.recall_total), 0) tot_accuracy
         FROM a, c
         WHERE a.actual_target_value = c.actual_target_value(+))
    SELECT 
    ROUND(d.tot_accuracy/GREATEST(0.0001, b.num_recalls) * 100, 4) as avg_accuracy,
    ROUND(GREATEST(0, ((1 - (1 - d.tot_accuracy/GREATEST(0.0001, b.num_recalls)) / GREATEST(0.0001, ((b.num_recalls-1)/GREATEST(0.0001, b.num_recalls)))) * 100)), 4) as predictive_confidence
    FROM b, d;

paragraphs.text:
%sql

-- Categorize the Predicted High Value Customers with respect to probability

SELECT COUNT(CUSTOMER_ID), range
FROM(
    SELECT CUSTOMER_ID,
          CASE
          WHEN probability >= 0 AND probability < 0.2 THEN 'Very Low Probability'
          WHEN probability > 0.2 AND probability < 0.4 THEN 'Low Probability'
          WHEN probability > 0.4 AND probability < 0.6 THEN 'Medium Probability'
          WHEN probability > 0.6 AND probability < 0.8 THEN 'High Probability'
          ELSE 'Very High Probability' END AS RANGE
        FROM HIGH_LTV_PREDICTED_V) t
    GROUP BY range;
